title: Not awaiting clarity before every beginning

captions.physics: Trying leisure through an unclear impression
captions.emotions: Feeling enjoyment remain at a standstill

meaning: A small free trial supports leisure when uncertain choice and waiting for a suitable moment leave both able to cross pleasure’s threshold.
text: Waiting can become stronger than the opportunity to rest itself. The Moon in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes tentative choosing through an unclear impression. The Hanged Man in energy leans towards suspended readiness. The Hanged Man in emotions leaves a feeling of stopping before joy. Repeated roles distinguish the delaying motive from its experience. A pause may offer another perspective when it restores a step. Otherwise both await clarity with no actual small experience through which clarity could appear.

For example, you seek a quiet evening activity and bring out a box of lovely shells. Looking at them or making an arrangement remains undecided. **A small trial can offer more clarity than waiting for the correct feeling.** You can pick up one shell and share an impression. It need not immediately begin a large programme. Discovering interest now permits freely continuing, choosing something else or finishing calmly without defining the whole meaning beforehand.

The difficulty is treating every doubt as reason to stop again. Conditions receive more discussion while available experience moves further away. Suspension is explained as care for a suitable beginning. Another view helps when permitting an imperfect trial. Free participation needs no final certainty. It can remain small and give a real answer that endlessly considering pleasures without inviting each other into a concrete step today cannot replace.
